objects.description: Opaque node type for the in-memory ASN.1 syntax tree used by libtasn1. Only a forward declaration is provided in this header; the structure is defined privately inside the library. Instances are obtained by parsing ASN.1 definitions or creating elements from a definitions tree. Destruction must be performed via the provided asn1_delete_structure APIs. Details of fields and layout are intentionally hidden.
Const-qualified pointer alias to an ASN.1 tree node. Used to denote read-only access to nodes managed by libtasn1. The underlying asn1_node_st is opaque.

On-disk/compiled representation of ASN.1 trees as produced by asn1_parser2array() and consumed by asn1_array2tree(). Each entry describes a node in a static array form with name, type (ASN1_ETYPE_*), and value pointer. The array is typically terminated by a special entry as per libtasn1 conventions.

Data holder used to read a node’s value from an asn1_node via asn1_read_node_value(). Carries the node name, a pointer to the value buffer (owned by libtasn1), its length, and the ASN1_ETYPE_* of the value.
Deprecated typedef for function return codes; it aliases int. New code should use int directly. Present for compatibility with older APIs.

functions.name: asn1_parser2tree
functions.signature: int asn1_parser2tree(const char *file, asn1_node *definitions, char *error_desc);
functions.description: Parses an ASN.1 specification from a file and builds an in-memory definition tree. Typical use is to load module definitions before creating or encoding/decoding elements. error_desc, if provided, may be populated on failure.
requirements: file must be a non-null path to a readable ASN.1 specification file.
definitions must be a non-null pointer to receive the created definition tree.
definitions must reference an uninitialized/as-null output (exact initialization requirements unknown).
error handling is via integer return code; caller should check the return value and, on failure, consult error_desc if provided.
Exact format and size requirements of error_desc are unknown (buffer size is not specified).

functions.name: asn1_parser2array
functions.signature: int asn1_parser2array(const char *inputFileName, const char *outputFileName, const char *vectorName, char *error_desc);
functions.description: Parses an ASN.1 specification file and writes an on-disk C array representation (asn1_static_node[]), suitable for embedding, to the output file, using vectorName as the C symbol. error_desc may be set on failure.
requirements: inputFileName must be a non-null path to a readable ASN.1 specification file.
outputFileName must be a non-null path where the generated C array will be written.
vectorName must be a non-null valid C identifier for the generated array symbol.
error handling is via integer return code; caller should check the return value and consult error_desc if provided.
Exact format and size requirements of error_desc are unknown (buffer size is not specified).

functions.name: asn1_array2tree
functions.signature: int asn1_array2tree(const asn1_static_node *array, asn1_node *definitions, char *errorDescription);
functions.description: Builds an in-memory ASN.1 definition tree from a static asn1_static_node array (typically produced by asn1_parser2array). errorDescription may be filled on failure.
requirements: array must be a non-null pointer to a valid asn1_static_node array; termination convention of the array is not specified here (commonly a terminating entry with type=ASN1_ETYPE_INVALID and NULLs, but exact requirement is unknown).
definitions must be a non-null pointer to receive the created definition tree.
Caller must check the integer return code and, on failure, may read errorDescription if provided.
Exact format and size requirements of errorDescription are unknown.

functions.name: asn1_print_structure
functions.signature: void asn1_print_structure(FILE *out, asn1_node_const structure, const char *name, int mode);
functions.description: Pretty-prints an ASN.1 structure or part of it to the given FILE stream. name selects a node/path to start printing (or possibly the whole structure), and mode controls the level of detail (e.g., names, types, values) using ASN1_PRINT_* constants.
requirements: out must be a valid FILE* open for writing.
structure must reference a valid ASN.1 node tree.
name may be NULL or a valid node path; exact semantics are not specified here.
mode must be one of the ASN1_PRINT_* constants defined in the header.

functions.name: asn1_create_element
functions.signature: int asn1_create_element(asn1_node_const definitions, const char *source_name, asn1_node *element);
functions.description: Creates a new ASN.1 element instance based on a type defined in the provided definitions tree. The created element is returned via element.
requirements: definitions must be a valid, initialized definitions tree created by parser functions.
source_name must be a non-null name of a type within definitions.
element must be a non-null pointer that will receive the created node.
Caller must check the integer return code before using the element.

functions.name: asn1_delete_structure
functions.signature: int asn1_delete_structure(asn1_node *structure);
functions.description: De-initializes and frees an ASN.1 element/structure. Intended to release resources for an element created or parsed.
requirements: structure must be a non-null pointer to an element handle to be deleted.
If *structure is non-null, it must refer to a valid libtasn1 node.
Caller should not use the element after successful deletion.
Caller must check the integer return code for success/failure.

functions.name: asn1_delete_structure2
functions.signature: int asn1_delete_structure2(asn1_node *structure, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Like asn1_delete_structure, with additional behavior controlled by flags. For example, ASN1_DELETE_FLAG_ZEROIZE zeroizes values before deinitialization.
requirements: structure must be a non-null pointer to a structure to delete.

functions.name: asn1_delete_element

functions.description: Removes a specific element (by path/name) from within an ASN.1 structure, deallocating that sub-node.
requirements: structure must reference a valid ASN.1 node tree.
element_name must be a non-null, valid path/name of an element within the structure.
Caller must check the return code and should not access the deleted element after success.

functions.name: asn1_write_value
functions.signature: int asn1_write_value(asn1_node node_root, const char *name, const void *ivalue, int len);
functions.description: Writes or updates the value of a node (selected by name path) within an ASN.1 structure. The semantics of ivalue and len depend on the target node type (e.g., integers, strings, OIDs).
requirements: node_root must be a valid ASN.1 node tree.
name must be a non-null path/name to the target node.

Caller must check the integer return code.

requirements: root must be a valid ASN.1 node tree.
name must be a non-null path/name to the target node.
ivalue must be a valid writable buffer when non-NULL.
len must be a non-null pointer; on input it should contain available buffer size, on output it is updated; exact in/out semantics and units depend on node type and are not fully specified here.
Caller must check the integer return code and handle insufficient buffer cases per return code conventions (exact values unknown).

functions.signature: int asn1_read_value_type(asn1_node_const root, const char *name, void *ivalue, int *len, unsigned int *etype);
functions.description: Reads a node's value as in asn1_read_value and also returns the node's value type (ASN1_ETYPE_*) via etype.
requirements: root must be valid.
name must be a non-null path/name.
ivalue may be a writable buffer; its required format/size depend on the node type (unknown specifics).

Caller must check the integer return code.

functions.description: Retrieves the raw data associated with a node into an asn1_data_node_st, including its name, value pointer, value length, and value type.

functions.description: Encodes an ASN.1 element (or a named sub-element) into DER. The encoded bytes are written to ider, and *len is used as in/out buffer length. ErrorDescription may be populated on failure.

len must be a non-null pointer; on input it should contain the buffer size, and on success it is updated to the number of bytes written.

functions.name: asn1_der_decoding2
functions.signature: int asn1_der_decoding2(asn1_node *element, const void *ider, int *max_ider_len, unsigned int flags, char *errorDescription);
functions.description: Decodes DER into an ASN.1 element, with additional control via flags. max_ider_len is used as in/out: on input, available bytes; on return, the number of bytes consumed. max_ider_len must be non-null; on input it contains the available length, on output it is updated to the number of bytes consumed.
flags must be a combination of ASN1_DECODE_FLAG_* values defined in the header.
Caller must check the return code and may consult errorDescription on failure; the size requirements for errorDescription are not specified.

# This generator targets fuzzing stubs that request:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(): expects a filename pointing to a file containing random fuzzable data.
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR(): used to build a C identifier (vectorName) for asn1_parser2array.
#
# We must provide one bytes buffer that the fuzzing harness will split across these
# FUZZ_PARAM_* calls. Common fuzzing frameworks concatenate multiple logical inputs
# into a single buffer and consume them in-order. We'll therefore encode our three
# logical inputs in a simple length-prefixed container:
#   [u16 len1][bytes filename1]
#   [u16 len2][bytes filename2]
#   [u16 len3][bytes identifier]
# Filenames should point to fuzzable data. Fuzzers typically map FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# to ephemeral files whose contents are set to the provided blob. To make that
# content interesting for libtasn1's asn1_parser2array (which parses ASN.1 specs),
# we will provide syntactically valid ASN.1 module text. We provide two different
# modules to exercise different parsing paths.
# The identifier must be a valid C identifier.
#
# Buffer size is kept <= 4096 bytes.

ASN1_MODULE_TEMPLATES: List[str] = [
    # Minimal valid module with a simple SEQUENCE and an OID
    """
    TestModule DEFINITIONS ::= BEGIN
    TestSequence ::= SEQUENCE {
      version INTEGER (0..255) DEFAULT 1,
      name    IA5String (SIZE(0..64)),
      flags   BIT STRING (SIZE(8)),
      id      OBJECT IDENTIFIER
    }
    id-test OBJECT IDENTIFIER ::= { iso(1) identified-organization(3) dod(6) internet(1) private(4) enterprise(1) 0 }
    END
    """.strip(),
    # Module with CHOICE, SET, ANY DEFINED BY pattern, and nested types
    """
    AdvancedModule DEFINITIONS ::= BEGIN
    AlgoId ::= OBJECT IDENTIFIER
    Param  ::= SEQUENCE {
      p INTEGER (0..65535),
      q INTEGER OPTIONAL
    }
    Payload ::= CHOICE {
      raw    OCTET STRING,
      number INTEGER,
      bits   BIT STRING (SIZE(0..32))
    }
    AnyWrap ::= SEQUENCE {
      oid AlgoId,
      any ANY DEFINED BY oid
    }
    Container ::= SET {
      items SEQUENCE (SIZE(1..3)) OF Payload
    }
    END
    """.strip(),
]

# A pool of valid OIDs to sprinkle into ASN.1 content if we want variability.
OIDS = [
    "1.2.840.113549.1.1.1",  # rsaEncryption
    "1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1",     # serverAuth EKU
    "2.5.4.3",               # commonName
    "1.2.840.10045.2.1",     # ecPublicKey
]

CIDENT_LETTERS = string.ascii_letters + "_"
CIDENT_TAIL = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"


def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 40) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    first = rng.choice(CIDENT_LETTERS)
    tail = "".join(rng.choice(CIDENT_TAIL) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return first + tail


def _rand_asn1_module(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rng.choice(ASN1_MODULE_TEMPLATES)
    # Optionally customize with an OID or tweak module name/identifiers to stay valid.
    # Keep it syntactically valid; simple substitutions only.
    mod_name = _rand_ident(rng, 6, 16)
    # Replace the first token ending with 'Module' or starting token with a custom name when found.
    # We'll simply prefix the module with our own name to ensure uniqueness.
    if "DEFINITIONS ::= BEGIN" in base:
        parts = base.split("DEFINITIONS ::= BEGIN", 1)
        lhs = parts[0].splitlines()[0]
        # Replace the module name (lhs) with our generated name, keeping the remainder intact.
        base = f"{mod_name} DEFINITIONS ::= BEGIN" + parts[1]
    # Randomly inject an OID definition at the end for variability.
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        oid = rng.choice(OIDS)
        extra = f"\ncustomOid OBJECT IDENTIFIER ::= {{ {oid} }}\n"
        if base.rstrip().endswith("END"):
            base = base.rstrip()[:-3] + extra + "END"
        else:
            base = base + extra
    return base


def _u16(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes([(n >> 8) & 0xFF, n & 0xFF])


def _pack_lp(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    if len(s) > 65535:
        s = s[:65535]
    return _u16(len(s)) + s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Create two filename payloads: each is an ASN.1 specification text.
    # FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME typically uses the content of the file at that path; the fuzzing
    # framework will map our provided bytes to that file's contents.
    asn1_a = _rand_asn1_module(rng).encode("utf-8")
    asn1_b = _rand_asn1_module(rng).encode("utf-8")

    # Ensure not exceeding the overall size budget when combined with identifier.
    # Reserve ~256 bytes for identifier and framing; trim if necessary.
    budget = 4096 - 256
    # Split budget roughly in half between the two files if needed.
    half = budget // 2
    if len(asn1_a) > half:
        asn1_a = asn1_a[:half]
    if len(asn1_b) > half:
        asn1_b = asn1_b[:half]

    ident = _rand_ident(rng, 3, 48).encode("ascii")

    blob = _pack_lp(asn1_a) + _pack_lp(asn1_b) + _pack_lp(ident)
    # Final guard: cap to 4096 bytes.
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4096]
    return bytes(blob)

def _gen_hidden(r: random.Random) -> str:

def _gen_with_spaces(r: random.Random) -> str:
    words = [

        _rand_choice(r, ["Project", "Data", "File", "Case", "Suite", "Example"]),

def _gen_path(r: random.Random, mode: int) -> str:
    gens = [
        _gen_rel_simple,
        _gen_rel_nested,
        _gen_abs_posix,
        _gen_hidden,
        _gen_with_spaces,
        _gen_edge_path,
    ]
    return gens[mode % len(gens)](r)


def _gen_name_simple(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return _rand_choice(r, [
        "",  # empty: often means root
        "root",
        "top",
        "certificate",
        "Subject",
        "Issuer",

def _gen_name_pathlike(r: random.Random) -> str:

    for i in range(depth):

            "notBefore", "notAfter", "serialNumber", "version", "name", "value"

        "*.*",

        s = _rand_component(r, 3, 10)

    return ".".join(parts)

        _gen_name_pathlike,
        _gen_name_wild,
        _gen_name_mixed,

    blob += _u16(len(name_b)) + name_b

# The target stubs use:
# - asn1_print_structure: needs a FILE* opened for writing (via FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME),
#   a name string (FUZZ_PARAM_STR), and an int mode from another param (not our buffer).
#   The structure input is provided by the fuzzing framework; our buffer should focus on
#   providing a valid filename and interesting name strings.
# - asn1_check_version: takes an optional version string; providing various plausible
#   version string formats increases coverage.
#
# The fuzzer framework will slice our bytes to provide separate values to FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME across calls. We therefore pack multiple plausible strings in
# one buffer using clear separators, so that extractions can yield valid data regardless
# of offset. We also include embedded NULs to terminate early if the fuzzer uses C-string
# semantics.
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce a short binary container that includes several NUL-terminated strings:
#   1) multiple plausible filenames (relative and absolute-like) with safe characters;
#   2) multiple plausible ASN.1 path/name strings (empty, simple, dotted, with indices,
#      with wildcards and quotes which libtasn1 often supports for node addressing);
#   3) several version-like strings e.g., "4.19", "4", "3.0", empty, random.
# - Interleave with separators (\n and NUL) to give the extractor multiple options.
# - Keep total size <= 4096.
# - Use seed to control randomness.

    parts = []

    rel2 = _random_component(rng)
    parts.append(f"{rel1}.bin")
    parts.append(f"{rel1}_{rel2}.dat")
    parts.append("out.der")
    parts.append("/tmp/fuzz_out.bin")
    parts.append("./fuzz.txt")
    parts.append("../f.out")

    base = [

# Basic DER helpers

def der_len(n: int) -> bytes:
    if n < 0x80:
        return bytes([n])
    # long form
    buf = []
    v = n
    while v > 0:
        buf.append(v & 0xFF)
        v >>= 8
    buf.reverse()
    return bytes([0x80 | len(buf)] + buf)


def der_tlv(tag: int, value: bytes) -> bytes:
    return bytes([tag]) + der_len(len(value)) + value


def der_null() -> bytes:
    return b"\x05\x00"


def der_octet_string(payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    return der_tlv(0x04, payload)


def der_bit_string(bit_bytes: bytes, unused_bits: int = 0) -> bytes:
    # BIT STRING value starts with unused-bits count byte
    return der_tlv(0x03, bytes([unused_bits]) + bit_bytes)


def der_integer(n: int) -> bytes:
    # Minimal two's complement
    if n == 0:
        enc = b"\x00"
    else:
        neg = n < 0
        v = abs(n)
        out = bytearray()
        while v:
            out.append(v & 0xFF)
            v >>= 8
        out.reverse()
        if not neg:
            # Ensure highest bit not set
            if out[0] & 0x80:
                out = bytearray(b"\x00" + bytes(out))
            enc = bytes(out)
        else:
            # Two's complement: extend to ensure MSB=1
            # Build positive then negate across width
            width = len(out)
            # If MSB already has high bit, keep width; else extend
            if out[0] & 0x80 == 0:
                out = bytearray(b"\x00" + bytes(out))
                width += 1
            # Invert
            out = bytearray((~b) & 0xFF for b in out)
            # Add 1
            carry = 1
            for i in range(width - 1, -1, -1):
                s = out[i] + carry
                out[i] = s & 0xFF
                carry = 1 if s > 0xFF else 0
            enc = bytes(out)
    return der_tlv(0x02, enc)


def encode_base128(value: int) -> bytes:
    # For OID arcs >= 128
    if value == 0:
        return b"\x00"
    parts = []
    while value > 0:
        parts.append(value & 0x7F)
        value >>= 7
    parts.reverse()
    for i in range(len(parts) - 1):
        parts[i] |= 0x80
    return bytes(parts)


def der_oid(oid: str) -> bytes:
    # Encode dotted-decimal OID
    arcs = [int(x) for x in oid.strip().split('.') if x]
    if len(arcs) < 2:
        arcs = [1, 3] + arcs
    first = 40 * arcs[0] + arcs[1]
    out = bytearray([first])
    for a in arcs[2:]:
        out += encode_base128(a)
    return der_tlv(0x06, bytes(out))

        if r.random() < 0.5:
            seg += "[" + rand_index(r) + "]"
        segs.append(seg)
    return ".".join(segs)


def common_names() -> List[str]:
    return [
        "a", "d", "s", "octet", "oid", "version", "serialNumber", "subject",
        "issuer", "extensions", "tbsCertificate", "signature", "publicKey",
        "algorithm", "parameters"
    ]


def make_der_set(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    out = []
    # OCTET STRING with small payload
    out.append(der_octet_string(r.randbytes(r.randint(0, 16))))
    # BIT STRING with a few bits
    bitlen = r.randint(0, 16)
    bytelen = (bitlen + 7) // 8
    unused = (8 - (bitlen % 8)) % 8
    out.append(der_bit_string(r.randbytes(bytelen), unused))
    # NULL
    out.append(der_null())
    # INTEGERs
    out.append(der_integer(r.randint(0, 2**31 - 1)))
    out.append(der_integer(r.randint(-2**31, -1)))
    # OID
    out.append(der_oid(r.choice(OID_POOL)))
    return out


def mix_lines_and_blobs(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    lines: List[bytes] = []
    # 1) A header with a recognizable marker
    lines.append(b"#asn1-inputs v1")

    # 2) Several path candidates
    for _ in range(r.randint(5, 10)):
        lines.append(make_path(r).encode('utf-8'))

    # 3) Common names and simple paths
    for name in common_names():
        lines.append(name.encode('utf-8'))
        lines.append((name + ".[0]").encode('utf-8'))

    # 4) Object identifier strings
    for oid in r.sample(OID_POOL, k=min(len(OID_POOL), r.randint(3, len(OID_POOL)))):
        lines.append(oid.encode('utf-8'))

    # 5) Type names often used with asn1_create_element (even if not directly here)
    type_names = [
        "Certificate", "TBSCertificate", "AlgorithmIdentifier", "SubjectPublicKeyInfo",
        "Attribute", "Name", "RelativeDistinguishedName", "Extension", "Validity"
    ]
    for t in type_names:
        lines.append(t.encode('utf-8'))

    # 6) Append several DER blobs preceded by a marker so consumers that read
    # as raw FUZZ_PARAM_STR still get valid binary if they happen to select these lines.
    ders = make_der_set(r)
    for i, blob in enumerate(ders):
        # Marker then raw bytes on the next line, keeping overall under MAX_OUT
        marker = f"DER[{i}]".encode('utf-8')
        lines.append(marker)
        lines.append(blob)

    # 7) Make a small constructed SEQUENCE of INTEGER + NULL to be used by decode functions
    seq_inner = der_integer(r.randint(0, 65535)) + der_null()
    seq = der_tlv(0x30, seq_inner)
    lines.append(b"DER[seq]")
    lines.append(seq)

    # 8) Another OCTET STRING that contains an encoded SEQUENCE (for expand_octet_string)
    inner = der_tlv(0x30, der_oid(r.choice(OID_POOL)) + der_null())
    lines.append(b"DER[octet-seq]")
    lines.append(der_octet_string(inner))

    # Join with newlines, truncating to MAX_OUT
    out = bytearray()
    for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
        if i != 0:
            nl = b"\n"
            if len(out) + len(nl) <= MAX_OUT:
                out += nl
            else:
                break
        if len(out) + len(ln) <= MAX_OUT:
            out += ln
        else:
            # Best-effort partial append for last line
            remain = MAX_OUT - len(out)
            if remain > 0:
                out += ln[:remain]
            break
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    return mix_lines_and_blobs(r)

# for the target fuzzers which request arbitrary strings/byte arrays via FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# We craft DER/BER-like encodings for common primitives to exercise encoders/decoders and
# meaningful payloads for asn1_write_value names and values.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Helpers for DER encoding of simple types (valid encodings)
def der_len(n: int) -> bytes:
    if n < 0:
        n = 0
    if n < 128:
        return bytes([n])
    out = bytearray()
    v = n
    while v > 0:
        out.append(v & 0xFF)
        v >>= 8
    out = bytes(reversed(out))
    return bytes([0x80 | len(out)]) + out

def der_tlv(tag: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    return bytes([tag]) + der_len(len(payload)) + payload

def der_null() -> bytes:
    return der_tlv(0x05, b"")

def der_boolean(val: bool) -> bytes:
    # Any non-zero content octet is TRUE; 0x00 is FALSE
    return der_tlv(0x01, b"\xFF" if val else b"\x00")

def int_to_twos_complement_bytes(x: int) -> bytes:
    if x == 0:
        return b"\x00"
    neg = x < 0
    v = -x if neg else x
    b = bytearray()
    while v:
        b.append(v & 0xFF)
        v >>= 8
    b = bytes(reversed(b))
    if not neg:
        # Ensure highest bit is 0 to keep positive
        if b[0] & 0x80:
            b = b"\x00" + b
    else:
        # Compute two's complement
        n = int.from_bytes(b, 'big')
        bits = 8 * len(b)
        maxv = 1 << bits
        twos = (maxv - n)
        t = twos.to_bytes(len(b), 'big')
        # Ensure highest bit is 1
        if not (t[0] & 0x80):
            t = (1 << (8*len(t))).to_bytes(len(t)+1, 'big')[1:]  # pad 0xFF-like
            # Recompute more directly using minimal negative encoding
            t = (int.from_bytes(b'\x01' + b, 'big') ^ ((1 << (8*(len(b)+1))) - 1) ) + 1
            t = t.to_bytes(len(b)+1, 'big')
            if not (t[0] & 0x80):
                t = b"\xFF" + t
        b = t
    return b

def der_integer(x: int) -> bytes:
    return der_tlv(0x02, int_to_twos_complement_bytes(x))

def der_octet_string(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return der_tlv(0x04, data)

def der_bit_string(bits: bytes, bit_len: int) -> bytes:
    # BIT STRING payload starts with number of unused bits in final octet
    total_bits = len(bits) * 8
    if bit_len < 0:
        bit_len = 0
    if bit_len > total_bits:
        bit_len = total_bits
    unused = (8 - (bit_len % 8)) % 8
    # Mask last byte's unused bits to zero for canonical encoding
    if len(bits) > 0 and unused:
        masked = bytearray(bits)
        masked[-1] &= (0xFF << unused) & 0xFF
        bits = bytes(masked)
    payload = bytes([unused]) + bits[: (bit_len + 7)//8]
    return der_tlv(0x03, payload)

def der_oid(arcs):
    # arcs: list of integers with at least 2 items
    if len(arcs) < 2:
        arcs = [1, 3]  # default to 1.3
    first = 40 * arcs[0] + arcs[1]
    body = [first] + arcs[2:]
    enc = bytearray()
    for i, v in enumerate(body):
        if i == 0:
            v0 = v
            # ensure valid base
            v = v0
        # base-128 with continuation bit
        stack = []
        if v == 0:
            stack = [0]
        else:
            while v > 0:
                stack.append(v & 0x7F)
                v >>= 7
        for j, b7 in enumerate(reversed(stack)):
            if j < len(stack) - 1:
                enc.append(0x80 | b7)
            else:
                enc.append(b7)
    return der_tlv(0x06, bytes(enc))

def der_ia5(s: str) -> bytes:
    data = s.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')
    return der_tlv(0x16, data)

def der_utf8(s: str) -> bytes:
    data = s.encode('utf-8')
    return der_tlv(0x0C, data)

def der_printable(s: str) -> bytes:
    allowed = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789 '()+,-./:=?"
    filt = ''.join(ch for ch in s if ch in allowed)
    return der_tlv(0x13, filt.encode('ascii'))

def der_sequence(items: list[bytes]) -> bytes:
    payload = b"".join(items)
    return der_tlv(0x30, payload)

def der_set(items: list[bytes]) -> bytes:
    payload = b"".join(items)
    return der_tlv(0x31, payload)

def rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:

def build_valid_der_samples(rng: random.Random) -> list[bytes]:
    samples = []

    # SEQUENCE of common pattern: AlgorithmIdentifier {OID, NULL}

    spk_bits = rng.randbytes(rng.randint(32, 128))

    tbs = der_sequence([

        tbs,
        alg,
        der_bit_string(rng.randbytes(rng.randint(64, 128)), rng.randint(64, 128)*8),

    samples.append(cert_like)
    # SET of attributes
    attrs = der_set([
        der_sequence([der_oid([2,5,4,3]), der_utf8(rng.choice(PRINTABLE_WORDS))]),
        der_sequence([der_oid([2,5,4,10]), der_utf8("ExampleOrg")]),
    ])
    samples.append(attrs)
    # Nested sequence
    nested = der_sequence([
        der_sequence([der_integer(1), der_boolean(True)]),
        der_sequence([der_octet_string(b"abc"), der_octet_string(b"def")]),
    ])
    samples.append(nested)
    return samples

def build_asn1_write_pairs(rng: random.Random) -> list[bytes]:
    # For asn1_write_value fuzzer, FUZZ_PARAM_STR is used twice: name and value independently.
    # We provide buffers that can serve as either a plausible name or a value.
    bufs = []
    # Names (ASCII paths)
    for _ in range(5):
        name = rng.choice(COMMON_NAMES)
        # sometimes add a dotted path or index-like suffix
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            name += "." + rng.choice(COMMON_NAMES)
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            name += ".?"  # some APIs use special tokens; harmless string here
        bufs.append(name.encode('ascii'))
    # OID strings as values
    for _ in range(3):
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            bufs.append(rng.choice(OID_STRINGS).encode('ascii'))
        else:
            # generate random dotted OID
            arcs = [rng.choice([0,1,2]), rng.randint(0, 39)] + [rng.randint(0, 200) for _ in range(rng.randint(0,6))]
            bufs.append(('.'.join(str(a) for a in arcs)).encode('ascii'))
    # Integers as ASCII decimal
    for v in [0,1,10,127,128,255,256,65535]:
        bufs.append(str(v).encode('ascii'))
    # Printable/UTF8 strings
    for _ in range(3):
        s = rng.choice(PRINTABLE_WORDS) + "-" + rand_ascii(rng, 3, 12)
        bufs.append(s.encode('utf-8'))
    # Raw binary blobs for OCTET STRING
    for _ in range(3):
        bufs.append(rng.randbytes(rng.randint(0, 64)))
    return bufs

def assemble_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> list[bytes]:
    corpus = []
    corpus.extend(build_valid_der_samples(rng))
    corpus.extend(build_asn1_write_pairs(rng))
    # Also include some combined DER constructs to reach different sizes
    # Chain sequences of previous items into a larger SEQUENCE, ensuring under 1024 each for stub.
    parts = rng.sample(corpus, k=min(5, len(corpus)))
    total_payload = b"".join(p[:128] for p in parts)  # cap size
    corpus.append(der_sequence([total_payload]))
    # Add a valid DER length-only blob for length parsers
    # e.g., an OCTET STRING with long-form length
    long_payload = rng.randbytes(rng.randint(130, 260))
    corpus.append(der_octet_string(long_payload))
    return corpus

def pick_buffer(rng: random.Random, corpus: list[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Bias towards medium length buffers that stubs cap at 1024
    choice = rng.choice(corpus)
    # Optionally pad with benign trailing bytes to vary size, but keep valid by wrapping in OCTET STRING
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        pad = rng.randbytes(rng.randint(0, 16))
        choice = der_octet_string(choice + pad)
    return choice[:1024]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    corpus = assemble_corpus(rng)
    buf = pick_buffer(rng, corpus)
    # Ensure result length bound for overall requirement
    return buf[:min(len(buf), MAX_TOTAL)]

# Helper: encode DER length
def der_len(n: int) -> bytes:
    if n < 0x80:
        return bytes([n])
    # long form
    out = []
    while n > 0:
        out.append(n & 0xFF)
        n >>= 8
    out.reverse()
    return bytes([0x80 | len(out)]) + bytes(out)

# Helper: DER INTEGER from signed Python int
def der_integer(val: int) -> bytes:
    # Two's complement minimal encoding
    if val == 0:
        content = b"\x00"
    else:
        neg = val < 0
        if neg:
            # compute minimal two's complement bytes
            # find minimal bytes that represent val
            # get absolute and build, then invert+add1 within width
            abs_v = -val
            b = bytearray()
            while abs_v:
                b.append(abs_v & 0xFF)
                abs_v >>= 8
            # determine width
            width = max(1, len(b))
            # extend to avoid sign confusion
            b += b"\x00"  # temporary to ensure space
            b = b[:width]
            # invert and add 1
            b = bytearray((~x) & 0xFF for x in b)
            carry = 1
            for i in range(len(b)):
                nv = (b[i] + carry) & 0xFF
                carry = 1 if b[i] + carry > 0xFF else 0
                b[i] = nv
            # ensure sign bit set
            if b[-1] & 0x80 == 0:
                b.append(0xFF)
            content = bytes(reversed(b))
        else:
            b = bytearray()
            vv = val
            while vv:
                b.append(vv & 0xFF)
                vv >>= 8
            b = bytearray(reversed(b))
            if b[0] & 0x80:
                b = bytearray(b"\x00") + b
            content = bytes(b)
    return bytes([0x02]) + der_len(len(content)) + content

# Helper: DER NULL
def der_null() -> bytes:
    return b"\x05\x00"

# Helper: DER BOOLEAN
def der_boolean(v: bool) -> bytes:
    return b"\x01\x01" + (b"\xFF" if v else b"\x00")

# Helper: DER OCTET STRING
def der_octet_string(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    return b"\x04" + der_len(len(data)) + data

# Helper: DER BIT STRING (with unused bits count)
def der_bit_string(bits: bytes, bit_len: int) -> bytes:
    # bits contains enough bytes to cover bit_len; pad last byte's unused bits to 0
    unused = (8 - (bit_len % 8)) % 8
    if len(bits) == 0 and bit_len == 0:
        payload = b"\x00"
    else:
        # mask off unused bits in last byte
        if len(bits) == 0:
            bits = b"\x00"
        b = bytearray(bits)
        if bit_len > 0:
            # index of last byte carrying data
            # ensure b has enough bytes
            need = (bit_len + 7) // 8
            if len(b) < need:
                b.extend(b"\x00" * (need - len(b)))
            last_index = need - 1
            mask = 0xFF & (0xFF << unused) if unused != 0 else 0xFF
            b[last_index] &= mask
            b = b[:need]
        payload = bytes([unused]) + bytes(b)
    return b"\x03" + der_len(len(payload)) + payload

# Helper: DER OBJECT IDENTIFIER from list of ints
def der_oid(components: List[int]) -> bytes:
    if len(components) < 2:
        components = [1, 0]
    first = 40 * components[0] + components[1]
    body = [first]
    for c in components[2:]:
        # base-128, MSB continuation
        enc = []
        if c == 0:
            enc = [0]
        else:
            while c > 0:
                enc.append(0x80 | (c & 0x7F))
                c >>= 7
            enc[-1] &= 0x7F
            enc.reverse()
        body.extend(enc)
    content = bytes(body)
    return b"\x06" + der_len(len(content)) + content

# Helper: DER UTF8String
def der_utf8(s: str) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode('utf-8')
    return b"\x0C" + der_len(len(b)) + b

# Helper: DER PrintableString (restrict to valid chars)
def der_printable(s: str) -> bytes:
    allowed = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789 '()+,-./:=?"
    s2 = ''.join(ch for ch in s if ch in allowed)
    b = s2.encode('ascii')
    return b"\x13" + der_len(len(b)) + b

# Helper: DER IA5String
def der_ia5(s: str) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode('ascii', 'ignore')
    return b"\x16" + der_len(len(b)) + b

# Helper: DER UTCTime (YYMMDDHHMMSSZ)
def der_utctime(year: int, mon: int, day: int, hh: int, mm: int, ss: int) -> bytes:
    yy = year % 100
    s = f"{yy:02d}{mon:02d}{day:02d}{hh:02d}{mm:02d}{ss:02d}Z"
    b = s.encode('ascii')
    return b"\x17" + der_len(len(b)) + b

# Helper: DER GeneralizedTime (YYYYMMDDHHMMSSZ)
def der_gentime(year: int, mon: int, day: int, hh: int, mm: int, ss: int) -> bytes:
    s = f"{year:04d}{mon:02d}{day:02d}{hh:02d}{mm:02d}{ss:02d}Z"
    b = s.encode('ascii')
    return b"\x18" + der_len(len(b)) + b

# Helper: SEQUENCE from list of already-encoded DER TLVs
def der_sequence(tlvs: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    content = b"".join(tlvs)
    return b"\x30" + der_len(len(content)) + content

# Helper: SET from list of TLVs
def der_set(tlvs: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    content = b"".join(tlvs)
    return b"\x31" + der_len(len(content)) + content

def build_name(r: random.Random) -> bytes:

# Build a small valid DER SEQUENCE mixing primitives

def build_mixed_sequence(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    pool = build_simple_tlv_pool(r)
    r.shuffle(pool)
    chosen = pool[:r.randint(2, min(6, len(pool)))]
    return der_sequence(chosen)

# Build an OCTET STRING that itself contains a valid DER SEQUENCE (useful for expanders)

def build_wrapped_der(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    inner = build_mixed_sequence(r)
    return der_octet_string(inner)

# Top-level constructor: choose among various structures

def build_der(r: random.Random, budget: int = 1024) -> bytes:
    choices = [
        build_mixed_sequence,
        build_name,
        build_spki,
        build_wrapped_der,
    ]
    # Also sometimes emit a single valid primitive TLV for length/tag decoders
    def single_primitive(rr: random.Random) -> bytes:
        return random.choice([
            der_integer(rr.randint(-1000, 1000)),
            der_octet_string(rr.randbytes(rr.randint(0, 64))),
            der_bit_string(rr.randbytes(rr.randint(0, 16)), rr.randint(0, 128)),
            der_oid([1, 3, 6, 1, 4, 1, rr.randint(1, 9999)]),
            der_null(),
        ])
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        blob = single_primitive(r)
    else:
        builder = r.choice(choices)
        blob = builder(r)
    # Ensure size bound
    return blob[:budget]

# Public API

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Slightly vary per call using additional jitter from PRNG
    _ = r.random()
    return build_der(r, budget=1024)

from typing import List

# Generator for ASN.1 type names used by asn1_create_element fuzz stub.
# The fuzz stub expects FUZZ_PARAM_STR to provide a type name present in the
# provided definitions tree. We cannot influence the in-memory definitions in
# this generator, but we can provide a palette of common ASN.1 type names and
# module-qualified names that are likely to exist in many test definitions.
# The output is a bytes buffer intended to be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
#
# Strategy:
# - Prefer well-known base types and typical application types.
# - Include COMMON aliases and case variations.
# - Include namespacing patterns like Module.Type and Module-Name.Type
# - Include structured types often present in PKIX (RFC 5280), CMS, PKCS #7.
# - Randomize selection but keep result valid identifier syntax.
# - Limit size to <= 4096 bytes (we produce short strings).
#
# The fuzzer harness will supply the definitions pointer and ensure it is a
# definitions tree. Our goal is to increase the chance that the chosen name
# matches a type defined in that tree.

BASE_TYPES = [
    "BOOLEAN", "INTEGER", "BIT STRING", "OCTET STRING", "NULL", "OBJECT IDENTIFIER",
    "UTF8String", "NumericString", "PrintableString", "TeletexString", "T61String",
    "IA5String", "UTCTime", "GeneralizedTime", "VisibleString", "BMPString",
    "UniversalString", "IA5String", "GraphicString", "ISO646String", "GeneralString",
    "RELATIVE-OID", "REAL", "ENUMERATED"
]

# Common module and type names often present in test suites and real-world specs
MODULE_NAMES = [
    "PKIX1Explicit88", "PKIX1Implicit88", "PKCS1", "PKCS7", "CMS", "X509", "X.509",
    "RFC5280", "TSP", "OCSP", "PKCS10", "CertificateExtensions", "Algorithm", "UsefulTypes",
    "Crypto", "MyModule", "TestModule", "ExampleModule", "ASN1C_Module"
]

COMMON_TYPES = [
    # X.509 / PKIX
    "Certificate", "TBSCertificate", "CertificateList", "RevokedCertificate",
    "TBSCertList", "CRL", "Name", "RDNSequence", "RelativeDistinguishedName", "AttributeTypeAndValue",
    "SubjectPublicKeyInfo", "AlgorithmIdentifier", "Validity", "Time", "SerialNumber",
    "Issuer", "Subject", "Extensions", "Extension", "GeneralName", "GeneralNames",
    "Version", "UniqueIdentifier", "BasicConstraints", "KeyUsage", "ExtendedKeyUsage",
    "AuthorityKeyIdentifier", "SubjectKeyIdentifier", "SubjectAltName", "IssuerAltName",
    "PolicyInformation", "CertificatePolicies", "CRLReason", "DistributionPoint",
    # CMS / PKCS7
    "ContentInfo", "SignedData", "EnvelopedData", "SignedAndEnvelopedData",
    "DigestedData", "EncryptedData", "SignerInfo", "RecipientInfo", "EncapsulatedContentInfo",
    # PKCS #10
    "CertificationRequest", "CertificationRequestInfo",
    # OCSP
    "OCSPRequest", "OCSPResponse", "ResponseData", "CertID",
    # TSP
    "TimeStampReq", "TimeStampResp",
    # Generic containers
    "SEQUENCE", "SET", "CHOICE", "ANY", "ANY DEFINED BY",
    # Misc
    "DigestAlgorithmIdentifiers", "Attributes", "Attribute",
]

# Some aliases/case variations frequently found
ALIASES = [
    "Type", "MyType", "My-Choice", "MySequence", "MySet", "Foo", "Bar", "Baz",
    "ISO646String", "INTEGER_0", "OCTET-STRING", "BIT-STRING",
]

# Optional module qualifiers and separator variants used in specs
SEPARATORS = [".", "-", "::"]

# Valid identifier cleanup: map spaces and hyphens to allowed forms commonly accepted
# in ASN.1 tools. libtasn1 typically allows spaces in canonical type tokens like
# "BIT STRING", but many type names are simple identifiers. We'll sometimes keep
# spaces for base types and sometimes compress them.

def maybe_compact(name: str, rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    if " " in name and rnd.random() < 0.5:
        # Keep canonical spaced name (e.g., BIT STRING)
        return name
    # Replace spaces with hyphen or remove
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        return name.replace(" ", "-")
    else:
        return name.replace(" ", "")


def qualify(name: str, rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Randomly prepend a module qualifier with different separators
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        mod = rnd.choice(MODULE_NAMES)
        sep = rnd.choice(SEPARATORS)
        return f"{mod}{sep}{name}"
    return name


def pick_type_name(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    bucket = rnd.random()
    if bucket < 0.35:
        base = rnd.choice(BASE_TYPES)
        base = maybe_compact(base, rnd)
        return base
    elif bucket < 0.8:
        t = rnd.choice(COMMON_TYPES)
        t = maybe_compact(t, rnd)
        # Sometimes qualify common types with a module
        return qualify(t, rnd)
    else:
        t = rnd.choice(ALIASES)
        t = maybe_compact(t, rnd)
        return qualify(t, rnd)


def add_suffix_variants(name: str, rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Add common suffixes like OPTIONAL choice names or version identifiers
    variants: List[str] = [name]
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        variants.append(name + "-v1")
    if rnd.random() < 0.2:
        variants.append(name + "-2023")
    if rnd.random() < 0.2:
        variants.append(name + "Ex")
    return rnd.choice(variants)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a shortlist of candidates and select one to keep output short but varied
    candidates = []
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 3)):
        n = pick_type_name(rnd)
        n = add_suffix_variants(n, rnd)
        candidates.append(n)

    # Prefer a single name (the stub only pulls one FUZZ_PARAM_STR for the type name)
    chosen = rnd.choice(candidates) if candidates else "Type"

    # Ensure it's a reasonable ASCII string; ASN.1 identifiers are typically ASCII
    s = chosen.encode('ascii', 'ignore')
    if not s:
        s = b"Type"

    # Return as bytes; the harness will use it for FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    return s[:4096]

import random
import re
from typing import List

# This generator produces a single bytes buffer intended to be consumed by
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR (as an OID dotted string) and FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) for flags.
# Strategy:
# - Compose a plausible OID dotted string covering various valid patterns:
#   * Short and long OIDs
#   * Different arc magnitudes (small, multi-byte base-128 when DER-encoded)
#   * Common prefixes (1.2, 2.5.4, 1.2.840, etc.)
#   * Edge arcs like 0, 39 (second arc boundary), large values (>= 16384)
# - Ensure no leading/trailing dot, no empty arcs, only digits and dots.
# - Optionally append a newline separator then a 4-byte little-endian flags value so
#   a harness that reads a single buffer can split; but typical fuzzer provides the
#   same buffer to different FUZZ_PARAM* calls, so we constrain to a single OID line.
#   The stub for asn1_object_id_der obtains flags from FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int), which
#   is separate from FUZZ_PARAM_STR, so we embed nothing extra here; only the OID text.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

COMMON_OID_PREFIXES = [
    [1, 2],                # 1.2
    [1, 3, 6, 1, 4, 1],    # 1.3.6.1.4.1 (enterprise)
    [2, 5, 4],             # 2.5.4 (X.520 attributes)
    [1, 2, 840],           # 1.2.840 (US)
    [1, 2, 840, 113549],   # 1.2.840.113549 (RSA)
    [1, 3, 6, 1, 5, 5, 7], # 1.3.6.1.5.5.7 (PKIX)
]

# Some interesting arc values to trigger multi-byte base-128 encodings and boundaries
INTERESTING_ARCS = [
    0, 1, 2, 3, 10, 16, 31, 32, 39, 40, 47, 63, 64, 127, 128, 129,
    16383, 16384, 65535, 65536, 2**31 - 1
]

def _rand_bool(r: random.Random, p: float) -> bool:
    return r.random() < p

def _pick_prefix(r: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.7):
        return list(r.choice(COMMON_OID_PREFIXES))
    # Random first two arcs must obey OID rule: first arc in {0,1,2} and
    # second arc 0..39 if first in {0,1}; if first == 2 then second can be large.
    first = r.choice([0, 1, 2])
    if first in (0, 1):
        second = r.randrange(0, 40)
    else:
        # Prefer interesting large values sometimes
        if _rand_bool(r, 0.5):
            second = r.choice([0, 39] + INTERESTING_ARCS)
        else:
            second = r.randrange(0, 2000)
    return [first, int(second)]

def _pick_arc(r: random.Random) -> int:
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.5):
        return int(r.choice(INTERESTING_ARCS))
    # Skew towards moderate values to stay valid while varying length
    return int(r.randrange(0, 50000))

def _build_oid(r: random.Random) -> str:
    arcs = _pick_prefix(r)

    # Decide total number of arcs: at least 2, up to ~16 to stay readable
    total = r.randrange(2, 17)
    while len(arcs) < total:
        arcs.append(_pick_arc(r))

    # Occasionally build well-known full OIDs
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.2):
        well_known = [
            [1, 2, 840, 113549, 1, 1, 1],   # rsaEncryption
            [1, 2, 840, 113549, 1, 1, 5],   # sha1WithRSAEncryption
            [2, 5, 4, 3],                   # commonName
            [2, 5, 4, 10],                  # organizationName
            [1, 3, 14, 3, 2, 26],           # sha1
            [1, 2, 840, 10045, 4, 3, 2],    # ecdsa-with-SHA256
            [1, 3, 6, 1, 5, 5, 7, 3, 1],    # serverAuth EKU
        ]
        arcs = r.choice(well_known)

    # Ensure arcs are non-negative integers
    arcs = [int(max(0, a)) for a in arcs]

    # Stringify without leading/trailing dots or empty arcs
    oid = ".".join(str(a) for a in arcs)
    # Clamp total size
    if len(oid) > 4000:
        oid = oid[:4000]
        # Trim possible trailing dot fragment to keep digits/dots only and no trailing dot
        oid = re.sub(r"\.+$", "", oid)
        oid = re.sub(r"\.+\.+", ".", oid)
        if not oid or "." not in oid:
            oid = "1.2"
    return oid


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Build an interesting OID dotted string
    oid = _build_oid(r)

    # Return only the OID text; FUZZ_PARAM_STR will consume this as std::string.
    # Keep ASCII digits and dots only.
    return oid.encode("ascii", errors="strict")
